title: Why structure comes first: a look at Structural Psychology

voices.name: Brian
voices.description: Deep and resonant, comforting and steady.

voices.name: Sarah
voices.description: Warm and reassuring, with a calm, confident delivery.

chapters.headline: Not the old structuralism
points: Not Wundt and Titchener's structuralism — that chapter of psychology's history is closed
A modern framework by Anita Kozlowski, developed since 2015 and published this year
"Structure" here means the architecture that governs what a mind can do
chapters.takeaway: The name is old; the framework is new — and structure means the architecture that governs the mind.

chapters.headline: Identity runs on an architecture of constraints
points: Identity is organized by a layered system of constraints — hierarchical necessity conditions
Beliefs, emotions, and behaviours are expressions of the structure, not its causes
Real change is architectural: recalibrate a governing condition and the change propagates
chapters.takeaway: Argue with a belief and you argue with a shadow; change the constraint and the outputs change.

chapters.headline: Content is downstream of structure
points: Psychology is fragmented by level; the framework claims the missing regulatory level
It aims at structure, not at the contents of the mind
Persistence is explained by necessity — what coherence costs — not by motivation
chapters.takeaway: Most psychology works on content; this framework works on the structure that admits the content.

chapters.headline: Why take it seriously
points: It names a real gap: no mainstream level explains how a person stabilizes
Its geometry matches how change actually behaves in organizations
It is stated precisely enough to disagree with — and to test
chapters.takeaway: Taking a framework seriously means engaging it at full strength — and asking what would count against it.

chapters.headline: Why it looks familiar from Axiovex
points: Axiovex planning is constraint-based: start from what must hold, search the admissible space
When a situation truly changes, a governing constraint changed — and everything downstream reorganized
Different domains, the same structural bet: the whole is what the constraints allow
chapters.takeaway: A person, like a plan, is what their governing constraints admit — structure comes first.
